Done. The two-kernel design splits LayerNorm across 256 chunks per batch element:

**Kernel 1 (`ln_reduce_kernel`)** — 4096 blocks (256 chunks × 16 batches), each block reduces 16,384 elements using shared-memory tree reduction and writes one (sum, sum_sq) pair to a small FP32 intermediate buffer.

**Kernel 2 (`ln_normalize_kernel`)** — same 4096-block grid. Every block independently reads all 256 partial sums for its batch, reduces them to global mean and inverse std, then normalizes its chunk of elements with the learned gamma/beta.

The result at [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge_no_examples/p40/round0/output_model_new.py) is 28x faster than the reference (0.139ms vs 3.85ms) on the MI300X, with 5/5 correctness passes.
